Retrieving data from OpenPrescribing

Source: vignettes/api.Rmd
api.Rmd

The code in this vignette needs network access to openprescribing.net. It is not run when the package is built, so no output is shown. The output layouts described are the ones the package tests check. Run op_check_api() first to confirm the API can be reached from your machine.

library(opamr)
op_check_api()

Organisation levels

org_type Level Example org
"national" England (the default) none
"regional_team" NHS England region "Y56"
"icb" Integrated Care Board "QWO"
"sicbl" Sub-ICB Location (formerly CCG) "02P"
"pcn" Primary Care Network "U12345"
"practice" GP practice "H81068"

Find codes by name:

op_org_search("Barnsley", "sicbl")
op_org_search("Densham", "practice")

Items, quantity and cost

op_spending() takes BNF codes at any level. OpenPrescribing sums everything under a code prefix, so "0501" gives all antibacterials and "0501013B0" gives amoxicillin.

nat     <- op_spending("0501013B0")                                        # England, all months
sub     <- op_spending("0501013K0", org_type = "sicbl", org = c("02P", "15N"))
all_sub <- op_spending("0501", org_type = "sicbl")                         # every Sub-ICB Location

Each call returns one row per code, organisation and month, with these columns:

date  org_type  org_id  org_name  code  items  quantity  actual_cost

op_spending_ab() does the same by antimicrobial. It looks up BNF codes with ab_to_bnf() and sums the chemicals that belong to one agent:

use <- op_spending_ab(c("amoxicillin", "nitrofurantoin", "doxycycline", "J01MA"))

Practices

The API returns every practice only one month at a time. Either list the practices, give a Sub-ICB code (which expands to its practices), or give date:

pr1 <- op_spending("0501", org_type = "practice", org = "02P")                     # practices in one Sub-ICB
pr2 <- op_spending("0501", org_type = "practice", date = c("2025-01", "2025-02"))  # every practice, two months

Each requested month is a separate request. Practice-level data for all of England over several years are large, so for bulk extraction the NHS Business Services Authority Open Data Portal (English Prescribing Dataset) is usually faster.

Denominators and rates

op_org_details() returns monthly list sizes and weighted denominators at any organisation level:

  • total_list_size: registered patients.
  • star_pu.oral_antibacterial_items: the STAR-PU weighting for oral antibacterial prescribing, which adjusts for the age and sex structure of the practice population.
  • astro_pu_items and astro_pu_cost: ASTRO-PU weightings.
den  <- op_org_details("sicbl", keys = c("total_list_size", "star_pu.oral_antibacterial_items"))
rate <- op_rate(all_sub, den, denominator = "star_pu_oral_antibacterial_items")

op_antibiotic_use() downloads prescribing and the denominator and computes the rate in one call:

amx_rates <- op_antibiotic_use("amoxicillin", org_type = "sicbl")                  # per 1,000 patients
op_plot_distribution(amx_rates, y = "rate", highlight = "02P")

Caching, rate limiting and retries

  • Responses are cached for the R session. To keep a cache across sessions, set a cache directory:

    options(opamr.cache_dir = "~/opamr-cache")

    Clear the cache with op_cache_clear(), for example after the monthly data release.

  • Requests are limited to 2 per second. Change this with options(opamr.rate = 1).

  • Transient failures (HTTP 429 and 5xx) are retried up to opamr.max_tries times (default 3).

  • If you get an error that the server returned an HTML page, a bot-protection layer has intercepted the request. This can happen on some networks. Try again later, from another network, or with a lower request rate.

Joining to resistance data

Sub-ICB Location codes in OpenPrescribing (org_id, such as "02P") are the same NHS organisation codes that appear at the end of Sub-ICB area names in UKHSA Fingertips (for example “South Yorkshire ICB - 02P”). This lets prescribing be joined to the Fingertips AMR local indicators by area and period. The sketch below assumes a Fingertips extract fp with columns area_name, period_start, count and denominator (the number of resistant isolates and the number tested). Check the area names and the boundary period before relying on the join.

fp$org_id  <- sub("^.* - ([A-Z0-9]{3})\\s*$", "\\1", fp$area_name)
fp$quarter <- as.Date(cut(fp$period_start, "quarter"))

use <- op_antibiotic_use("trimethoprim", org_type = "sicbl")
use$quarter <- as.Date(cut(use$date, "quarter"))
q_use <- aggregate(cbind(items, total_list_size) ~ org_id + quarter, data = use, FUN = sum)
q_use$rate <- q_use$items / q_use$total_list_size * 1000

joined <- merge(fp, q_use, by = c("org_id", "quarter"))

Points to check before modelling:

  • Boundaries. Sub-ICB Locations replaced CCGs in July 2022, and several merged in 2025, so a code’s population can change over time.
  • Monthly versus quarterly sums. The quarterly sum of monthly list sizes is about three times the average list size. That does not affect the rate above, because both items and list size are summed over the same three months.
  • Rolling indicators. Many Fingertips resistance indicators are rolling averages. Use the discrete quarterly ones if you want counts that can be modelled.
